title: Presidential New Year citizen question-and-answer event
reason: Official civic forum, not a reported protest action.
notes: Search-only discovery describes a presidential New Year event where citizens addressed questions to the head of state. It does not report a collective protest, protest demand, or participant count.

title: Teacher-union strike threat over professional assessment
reason: Conditional strike threat and policy dialogue; no executed protest gathering is established.
notes: IWACU’s 15 January body reports that teachers threatened to begin a strike after dialogue over the planned professional assessment failed; it does not say the strike started or describe a public gathering. Search-only January ministry and later RFI/US State Department summaries mention suspension or an announced strike movement and presidential threats, but do not establish attendance or an executed protest. Teacher membership counts are not event attendance. The February agreement is retained separately as a boundary follow-up.

title: Ntega workers and traders object to proposed local contributions for substitute teachers
reason: Policy objections reported without an executed public assembly or protest.
notes: The opened SOS Médias report describes objections to a proposed local contribution and asks for union intervention. The contribution was planned to begin later in January; the article does not document implementation, a strike, gathering, participant count, or protest response. Official threats reported in the article do not establish a response to an assembly.

title: Students and educators ask REGIDESO to repair a school transformer
reason: Search-only utility-service complaint; no public protest gathering is described.
notes: The Radio Inzamba search result says students and educators asked the public utility to repair a transformer. It provides no verified event form, participant count, or protest date; a service complaint alone does not establish a qualifying assembly.

title: Gitaza residents report forced porterage by soldiers
reason: Rights complaint and reported coercion, not a documented protest assembly.
notes: A Radio Inzamba search result reports residents complaining that soldiers compelled them to carry goods. No collective protest action, gathering, attendance, or protest demand is described.

title: Bujumbura fuel shortage and transport disruption
reason: Shortage impacts and passenger complaints do not establish collective protest action.
notes: Search-only RPA and SOS Médias reports describe fuel scarcity and disruption to public transport. They do not identify a public gathering, protest turnout, or a collective demand directed at the Burundian state.

title: Kwa Siyoni traders stop work over stand-rent increases
reason: Private-owner rent dispute and business stoppage; no distinct qualifying public assembly or state-policy target is documented.
notes: Contemporary IWACU and SOS Médias bodies report closed businesses with traders present at their stands from 25 January and at least into 26 January. The collective demand is directed to the private market owner/management. The reported population of more than 5,000 traders is not strike attendance; no participant count or separate public assembly is documented. One IWACU story mentions taxes as operating expenses but does not identify a collective demand to change state policy. Yaga’s 2023 retrospective confirms the market’s private ownership context only. No exact physical end or state response is established. This remains separate from the old Central Market reconstruction grievance in X008.

title: Public frustration over promised reconstruction of the former Bujumbura Central Market
reason: Search-only reporting describes a public-policy grievance but no January protest action or gathering.
notes: The 27 January RPA search result says citizens and former traders still awaited government-promised reconstruction after the 2013 fire and reports public frustration with authorities. It does not describe a January assembly, commemoration, protest action, or turnout. The two host variants are one story, not independent corroboration. Keep this possible government-directed grievance separate from the Kwa Siyoni private-rent stoppage in X007.

title: UCEDD association meeting mentioned in monthly rights monitoring
reason: Search-only internal association meeting and detention lead; no qualifying public protest is established.
notes: The SOS-Torture monthly bulletin search result mentions an association meeting and detention context. The report body was not reviewed, and the excerpt does not establish a public-policy protest assembly or turnout.
